title: Route Visualizer: Fallback Variant Scenario Walkthrough
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Enable customers to author, validate, and preview routing policies that include region selection, tier routing, and automatic fallback model variants via an interactive Route Visualizer. The visualizer should let users craft a scenario (region + tier weights + traffic shift over time + fallback rules), run a simulated preview that reports latency/cost/regression risk, and export the scenario as a reusable playbook. This ticket covers the PM-facing definition, acceptance criteria, stakeholder alignment, and required artifacts for the UX/eng implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Visual scenario builder: users can create a scenario with at least one region, two tiers, and one fallback variant rule and save it as a named scenario.
Traffic timeline: users can specify time-based traffic shifts (eg. 80% us-west -> 20% eu-west over a 30-minute window) and the preview shows how routing decisions change over time.

Preview metrics: preview must surface estimated end-to-end p50/p95 latency, per-token cost delta, estimated SLO breach probability, and a simple quality regression score relative to a baseline model variant.
Validation linter: editor warns for unsafe policies (circular fallbacks, unreachable tier, region without capacity) with explainable fixes and suggested quick actions.
Fallback testing: the preview can simulate a model-variant failure and demonstrate automatic fallback with timings and observed metric changes.
Export/playbook: scenarios can be exported as JSON playbooks and imported back into the Policy Studio for reuse or automated rollout jobs.
Telemetry links: preview includes links to the runtime telemetry dashboard and a synthetic traffic replay log for the scenario.
Security: no sensitive customer data is included in scenario exports; KMS-protected artifacts are referenced where appropriate.
Documentation: console docs updated with a step-by-step walkthrough and example playbooks (docs link provided).
updates_comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with ENG/Design. Agreed scope: visual timeline + fallback sim + linter. ENG to prototype timeline UI.
2026-03-04: Design review - removed complex conditional branching UI for MVP; replaced with tier weight sliders + fallback priority list.
2026-03-06: ENG spike completed (ENG-82412). Prototype shows timeline scrubber and live metric estimation using sampling of historical latencies.
2026-03-08: UX feedback from customer success: include a cost delta estimate and an explanation of quality regression score. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10: Security review note: exports must strip API keys and reference KMS-encrypted model ids. Marking security_review_required=false for console export; infra will handle keys.
decision_log: Keep simulation client-side for small scenarios to allow offline previews, but run server-side full-sim for enterprise-sized traffic to use historical telemetry.
Quality regression score will be a weighted diff against baseline prompts using the customer's saved eval set or a Redwood default set.
MVP will support region selection + tier weights + single fallback priority chain. Complex conditional branching deferred to later cycle.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Preview metrics could be misleading if historical telemetry is sparse. Mitigation: show confidence bands and require a minimum sample size warning.
Risk: Exported playbooks may expose model identifiers. Mitigation: replace identifiers with stable aliases and require KMS access to decrypt when applying playbooks.
Risk: UI complexity could overwhelm new users. Mitigation: provide a Guided Walkthrough mode and a one-click 'Safe Defaults' template.
qa_plan: Create a suite of scenario fixtures (small, medium, large) and run preview consistency tests comparing client-side quick-sim with server-side full-sim.
E2E test: set up a synthetic traffic replay (observability link) and validate that the simulated fallback times align with runtime logs within tolerance.
Accessibility: timeline scrubbing and sliders must be keyboard operable and have ARIA labels.
next_steps: ENG: implement timeline UI prototype and expose simulation API (ENG-82412).
Design: produce final mocks for export/playbook modal and linter messages by 2026-03-12.
PM: prepare customer-facing walkthrough and two example playbooks for GA demos.
Set up a short customer beta with 3 enterprise accounts to validate preview accuracy and UX.
